scores.evidence_span: international options included only when their incremental value is compelling
scores.rationale: This implies attention to value, but does not explicitly state ROI or cost-effectiveness as a decision priority.
No research source or evidence class is identified for evaluating ROI or cost-effectiveness.
No named option is supported by a verifiable cost-effectiveness fact.
No named option or route has a concrete fact establishing its expensive, prestige-oriented character.
The report does not compare cost-effective routes with expensive prestige-oriented programs.
No learning option is recommended because of its ROI or cost-effectiveness.
No otherwise viable option is downgraded for prioritizing expensive prestige.
The report provides clarification questions rather than an executable plan step implementing cost-effectiveness.
The hypothetical budget is not a cost-effectiveness allocation rule, and 'incremental value is compelling' supplies no usable threshold or checkpoint.
No concrete condition establishes when expensive prestige-oriented programs would become the better choice.
There is no evidence-backed chain connecting cost-effectiveness to a decision or action.
